criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First two lines stand alone, name the mechanism (submarine cable landing rules) and the concrete news trigger (July 8, 2026, DA-26-684), and land the AK stake (GCI Liberty/Quintillion, only Arctic fiber). Signals a correction ('who can close') without snark. Docket cite in line 1 slightly crowds the ~210-char cutoff but it still works.

criteria.name: Mechanism load-bearing + AK consequence
criteria.notes: Mechanism genuinely drives an AK underwriting decision. Concrete consequence: sector (connectivity substrate for North Slope/Railbelt AI data centers), named actor (Quintillion as only U.S.-Arctic subsea operator), decision/risk (delay-or-reprice), and timeframe (early-2027 in-service). Both sides fully carried.

criteria.name: Layer fidelity
criteria.notes: All four body layers appear in the dossier with matching controlling actors (FCC under 1921 Act, OIA on OI Docket 24-523, full Commission FCC 25-49, Committee/AG). Chain is complete and readable; no invented layers. Actors summarized tightly and accurately rather than verbatim.

criteria.name: Chokepoint clarity
criteria.notes: Names ONE specific layer (the fourth), the actor (Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation chaired by the AG), and the true binary (file an objection vs. return no objection and let the FCC grant). Asymmetric, not a diffuse Congress-style veto. Mention of Defense/Homeland Security as members marginally softens the single-actor framing.

criteria.name: Structural read
criteria.notes: Takes a real, honest position ('the visible regulator is not the gate'; reprice/block authority parked in a DOJ-chaired committee invisible on the docket surface) grounded in how the referral machinery actually works. Proportionate, not a flat explainer, matches the dossier's structural read.

criteria.name: Forward implication
criteria.notes: Names a concrete next move: treat Team Telecom clearance (not the FCC grant) as the binding closing condition, stress-test schedule/financing against a mitigation-agreement scenario vs. an unconditional early-2027 date. Cites the referral dates (Feb 17 / Mar 20, 2026). Actionable this week; who carries risk is named.

criteria.name: Primary-source quality
criteria.notes: Every layer traces to a primary source in the dossier (FCC public notices DA-26-684/DA-26-296, Report and Order FCC 25-49, OI Docket 24-523, docketed application SCL-MOD-20250930-00070). Chokepoint citation is primary. Unverified dollar figures correctly excluded.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, position-taking, structural, business-literate, Alaska-first; breaks machinery down in plain language without losing sophistication. Not explainer-bot or influencer cadence. Minor stretches ('reprice-or-block authority is parked') read slightly dense but stay on voice.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Word count (435) and char count are in-window, paragraphs are tight (2-4 sentences), scans well. The bullet block is well-formed but the four items are multi-sentence rather than the single-clause items the top descriptor rewards, so it is slightly heavier to scan than ideal.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Closes with a real, debatable question tied directly to the chokepoint (if the Committee objects on the Quintillion referral, who carries the repriced risk, buyer/lenders/offtaker). No CTA, no rhetorical softener. On-topic and specific.

one_sentence_fix: Tighten each of the four layer bullets to a single clause (move the descriptive second sentences into the surrounding prose) so the bullet block scans as clean single-clause items on mobile.
